title: What happens when a bank transfer is sent?
sources: Nacha Automated Clearing House Operating Rules

lines.text: Why does sending a message to the other side of the planet take one second, but a bank transfer takes three business days?
lines.caps: Why do bank *transfers | take three full *days?

lines.text: It is not because the computers are slow; it is due to a fifty-year-old banking architecture called ACH.
The Automated Clearing House was designed in the nineteen-seventies to replace physical paper checks.
lines.caps: Created in the 1970s to *replace | physical paper *checks

lines.text: Instead of settling transactions instantly, banks bundle transfers into giant batches processed only a few times a day.
lines.caps: Banks bundle transfers into *giant | batches a few times *daily

lines.text: Transfers flow to the Federal Reserve, which verifies reserve funds and settles debits overnight.
lines.caps: The Federal Reserve *clears | and settles balances *overnight

lines.text: The three-day lag also allows banks to catch fraudulent overdrafts, while earning interest on funds in transit.
lines.caps: The lag lets banks check *fraud | and earn interest on *float!

lines.text: New real-time networks like FedNow are finally bringing instant transfers into the modern age.
lines.caps: Real-time payment *rails | are finally making money *instant!
